subject: Bastion Edge + Vault TLS Handoff: FQDN delegation & rotation cadence
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Martin O'Neil <martin@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: CloudOps Eng <cloudops@acme-cloud.com>
Date: 2028-07-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Bastion Edge + Vault TLS Handoff: FQDN delegation & rotation cadence

Hi team,

Following our quick sync this morning, I'm putting together a concise handoff for the on-prem bastion/edge that will front private-hosted Redwood nodes in Acme's VPC. Main goals:
- Clarify who will own the private FQDN(s) and the exact DNS delegation window.
- Agree the TLS termination point for inbound connections (edge vs. internal proxy).
- Finalize certificate rotation cadence and how Vault/HSM-backed keys are presented to the runtime.

Action items I propose (see attached handoff matrix):
1) Acme to create a stub-zone/delegation for: bastion-prod.acme.internal -> delegate to redwood-edge.{region}.svc (we'll provide NS). Window: 2-3 hours during maintenance window.
2) Decide TLS termination model: we recommend mutual-TLS at the edge (client cert from Acme services) with optional re-encryption to internal services using certs signed by Redwood's internal CA. This gives workload isolation while keeping validation at the edge.
3) Certificate rotation: Vault (Acme) will host the private key in HSM and provide signed certs via CSR endpoint. Rotation cadence: quarterly by default; emergency rotation 48hrs. We will need the CSR signing endpoint URL and contact person.

Please review the attached redwood-acme-handoff-matrix.csv and the proposed tls-rotation-schedule.xlsx. Karthik / Laura — can you confirm whether the runtime requires SANs for per-tenant FQDNs or a wildcard is acceptable for now? Also flag any constraints on our side for mTLS CA pinning.

Martin — can you confirm the preferred maintenance window (dates/times) and whether Acme's ops team will perform the zone change or if you'd prefer Redwood's infra SRE to do it under your guidance?

Thanks,

Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood-acme-handoff-matrix.csv (CSV, 1.2KB), tls-rotation-schedule.xlsx (Excel, 12KB)
From: Martin O'Neil <martin@acme-cloud.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudOps Eng <cloudops@acme-cloud.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bastion Edge + Vault TLS Handoff: FQDN delegation & rotation cadence

Thanks Alex — useful summary. A few clarifying points from Acme: 

- Maintenance window: we prefer Tue/Wed 0200-0500 UTC. That works for our DNS TTLs and change control.
- Delegation: Acme is comfortable creating a delegating NS record pointing to the hosts you give us, but we need the exact NS IPs and the forwarding TTL the day before. Can Redwood provide a cutover checklist?
- mTLS: Our services currently prefer client certs issued by Acme's internal PKI; we can provide a CA bundle for verification at the edge. Can Redwood's edge accept multiple CA roots (Acme + Redwood for cross-test traffic)?
- HSM/Vault: We run HashiVault (enterprise) with an HSM-backed key. We can expose a CSR signing endpoint behind a private URL. We'll need a short proof-of-possession flow (signed nonce) to validate calls.

Two asks:
1) Please include an explicit fallback plan in case the delegation cutover fails (how do clients reach Redwood during rollback?).
2) Confirm whether Redwood requires SANs for client certs when we do per-service provisioning; we prefer short-lived SANed certs issued per-service.

Martin
Martin O'Neil
Head of CloudOps, Acme Cloud
martin@acme-cloud.com
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Martin O'Neil <martin@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-30T13:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bastion Edge + Vault TLS Handoff: FQDN delegation & rotation cadence

Good questions — thanks. Quick answers inline: 

- Maintenance window: Tue/Wed 0200-0500 UTC works for Redwood SRE as well. We'll aim to perform the final NS cutover at the start of the window and validate traffic for the first hour.
- NS list: attached (see handoff CSV) includes the cluster-facing NS names and public IPs. We'll provide a final 'go/no-go' checklist 24 hours prior.
- Multiple CA roots: yes, the edge can be configured to trust multiple client CA roots. We'll support Acme's PKI certificate bundle; we will also present Redwood's CA when Redwood-originated control calls are made. We'll document the verification logic in the Confluence page.
- Proof-of-possession: acceptable. We'll provide a short HMAC nonce exchange flow for CSR submission; if Acme's Vault supports signed nonces (it does), we'll use that for enrollment.

Fallback plan (summary):
- If delegation fails or validation errors exceed threshold, we will revert NS delegation and route clients to a short-lived TCP/TLS proxy that accepts legacy hostnames (IP-based) for 24 hours. That proxy increments logging and requires an alternate auth header (X-Backup-Auth) — we'll provide instructions in the cutover playbook.

SANs vs Wildcard:
- Runtime prefers exact SANs for per-tenant isolation (routing and certificate pinning). Wildcard can be used temporarily, but SANed certs are recommended for production. If Acme is issuing short-lived SANed certs per-service, Redwood runtime can accept them without changes.

Next steps:
- Laura: can you draft the final cutover checklist and the 'rollback' proxy config snippets?
- Karthik: can you size any config changes needed to accept multiple CA bundles at the edge and confirm if config reload is hot or requires restart?

I'll update Confluence with the agreed items and a proposed cutover date (next Tue).

Alex
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-30T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bastion Edge + Vault TLS Handoff: FQDN delegation & rotation cadence

Quick from infra: edge accepts multiple CA bundles via dynamic truststores; reload is hot via SIGHUP to the edge-agent and does not impact in-flight connections (we hot-reload PEM bundles). We'll add support for validating signed nonces on the CSR endpoint — small change, no restart.

On SANs: runtime routing table uses CN/SAN to map tenant -> KV-cache shard; SANed certs are preferred. Wildcard is OK for initial testing but will complicate debugging/log aggregation.

I'll post a diff to the deployment repo with the small truststore acceptance change and a sample systemd unit annotation for the SIGHUP flow.

Karthik
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Martin O'Neil <martin@acme-cloud.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-31T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Bastion Edge + Vault TLS Handoff: FQDN delegation & rotation cadence

Perfect — thanks everyone. Laura and I will finalize the cutover checklist and the rollback proxy snippet by EOD today and attach it to the Confluence page. Martin, please confirm the final NS list by EOD Tomorrow and we'll lock the Tuesday window.

Deliverables before cutover:
- Final handoff matrix (attached) — Laura/Alex
- Confluence cutover playbook with rollback steps — Laura
- CSR nonce exchange spec and sample call — Karthik
- Acme to provide CA bundle, CSR URL, and 'go/no-go' contact — Martin

If there are no objections, we'll treat this as the cutover plan and schedule the change ticket.

Thanks,
Alex
